paragraphs: A cinema prime is a heavy cylinder covered in scales. The focus and iris rings carry marked gear teeth for follow focus units, the front is a large diameter thread for filters, and the mount at the back is a locking bayonet rather than a screw. Those rings and the marks on them are what identify it as cinema rather than stills glass.
The mesh is efficient at 58,110 polygons and 32,080 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the gear rings, the barrel steps and the mount.
At $29 it suits camera and cinema equipment visualisation, rental house and manufacturer catalogues, film production set dressing, technical marketing and games. On sale since 2022.

A twin filament headlamp bulb is a small object with a lot of precision in it: two filaments at different positions, a shield under one of them to cut the beam, a glass envelope with a blackened tip and a metal base with locating tabs that only fit one way. Those tabs are why the beam pattern is repeatable.

The mesh is light at 9,280 polygons and 9,299 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the glass, the metal base and the printed markings.

At $29 and built to StemCell specification, it suits automotive parts marketing and catalogues, workshop and service visualisation, technical illustration, retail renders and games. On sale since 2021.

A basketball vest has almost no construction: wide armholes, a deep neckline, side seams and nothing else. That means all of the shape comes from how it hangs on a body, and the design work is entirely in the print - the numbers, the team name and the trim along the openings.
The mesh is minimal at 3,808 polygons and 3,801 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 3 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the mesh fabric structure and the print.

White and black versions sit on this page at the same $29. All suit sports visualisation and broadcast graphics, team kit and apparel retail renders, character set dressing and games. On sale since 2016.

A campfire is a small architecture: logs leaned or stacked so air moves through the middle, a ring of stones, ash and embers below and flame between the wood rather than on top of it. That internal structure is what makes a fire believable - flames coming off a solid pile look wrong immediately.
The mesh is light at 9,001 polygons and 9,035 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the logs as separate bodies and the geometry spent on the charring and the stack arrangement.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits camping and outdoor visualisation, travel and adventure advertising, evening and night scenes, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2024.

A stylised building is a design exercise in reduction: keep the columns, the pediment and the coins-on-the-sign that say bank, and throw away everything else. Proportions get exaggerated deliberately, because the shape has to read at a glance in a game or an explainer where nobody stops to look.
The mesh is light at 29,378 polygons and 16,310 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly the budget a stylised asset should carry - simple forms and flat colour.

Red and green versions sit on this page at the same $29. All suit games and interactive media, explainer and motion graphics, financial and educational content, children's material and print. On sale since 2022.

A cedar of Lebanon grows outward rather than upward once it matures: the trunk divides low, and the branches spread into flat horizontal plates of foliage stacked one above another. That tiered silhouette is entirely unlike a young conifer and is what makes the species recognisable across a landscape.
The mesh runs 260,393 polygons and 247,163 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the deeply fissured bark and the foliage plates.
At $29 it suits landscape and architectural visualisation, garden and estate renders, heritage and cultural material, film and television, and games. On sale since 2022.

Browline glasses put a thick top rim over a thin wire lower frame, which is why they read as half spectacle and half eyebrow. Clear acetate makes that construction visible rather than hiding it, and it also means the model has to handle a transparent frame over transparent lenses without either disappearing.
The mesh is light at 10,694 polygons and 10,716 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the brow, the hinges and the nose bridge.

At $29 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits eyewear retail and e-commerce renders, fashion and lifestyle visualisation, character set dressing for film, television and games, and advertising. Real-world scale is kept, so they fit a standard head. On sale since 2025.

Detachable controllers are an unusual design problem: each half has to work alone in a hand, attach to a console, and pair with its mirror image to form a conventional pad. That triple duty is why the shapes are asymmetric, why the rails run down the inner edge, and why the buttons sit where they do.
The models are built in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the two halves as separate bodies so they can be shown attached, detached or held in either configuration.

At $29 and built to StemCell specification, it suits gaming hardware advertising, consumer electronics visualisation, product and e-commerce renders, desk and living room scenes, and games. On sale since 2025.

A crushed can is far more useful than an intact one for the same reason a crumpled bag is: bins, gutters, recycling scenes and desk clutter all need packaging that has been used. Each can folds differently depending on how it was crushed, which is why a set beats a single item repeated.

The mesh runs 18,886 polygons and 18,048 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry entirely spent on the deformation, and ships with 6 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the printing distorted across the folds.
At $29 it suits recycling and waste visualisation, urban and street set dressing, interior clutter, sustainability material, film and television, and games. On sale since 2016.

A cyclorama flood is a wide asymmetric fixture used to light a curved white wall evenly from top to bottom, and the four bank version stacks four cells in one housing so each can carry a different colour. That arrangement is why the fitting is so long and why the reflector shape looks lopsided.
The model is built with clean non-overlapping surfaces so the reflector, the housing and the colour frames can each take their own material treatment.

At $29 it suits theatre and studio lighting visualisation, television and photographic studio interiors, lighting equipment marketing and catalogues, production set dressing and games. On sale since 2016.

The double fisherman's is the knot used to join two ropes when the join must never come undone: two strangling knots that jam against each other under load. Modelling it correctly means the two halves have to mirror and interlock exactly, because anyone who ties knots will see immediately if the lay is wrong.

The model is built with subdivision geometry at 1,392 polygons and 1,452 vertices with non-overlapping UVs. Subdivision is the right choice for rope: the strands stay round and smooth however close the camera gets.
At $29 it suits climbing and outdoor sports visualisation, safety and rescue training material, sailing and rigging illustration, technical and educational content, and games. On sale since 2021.

A police duty belt is a load bearing platform: a wide leather or nylon belt with keepers holding it to the trouser belt, and a set of pouches, holster and equipment loops spaced around it in an order that matters because everything has to be reachable without looking.

The mesh is minimal at 3,340 polygons and 3,386 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 4096x4096 carrying the leather grain, the stitching and the hardware.

At $29 it suits law enforcement and security visualisation, character set dressing for film, television and games, equipment presentation and training material. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard figure. On sale since 2020.

A grid battery unit is a shipping container sized enclosure with cooling equipment along one side, ventilation grilles and connection points at one end. It is designed to be craned into place and wired up rather than built on site, which is why it looks like industrial packaging rather than like a building.
The mesh runs 112,480 polygons and 117,808 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the cooling units, the door panels and the base frame.

At $29 and built to StemCell specification, it suits renewable energy and grid visualisation, utility and infrastructure presentation, investor and trade material, planning documents and games. On sale since 2024.

A large water bottle is engineered as much as designed: the ribs around the body are there to stop the thin walls collapsing, the base has a moulded pattern to take the pressure, and the neck carries a tamper ring under the cap. Those details are what separate a real bottle from a smooth cylinder.
The mesh is efficient at 17,345 polygons and 18,640 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the ribbing, the base pattern and the cap.
At $29 it suits beverage packaging visualisation, brand and label mockups, supermarket and e-commerce renders, food photography set dressing, and games. On sale since 2021.
